interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) diagnosis with pathological stage pT3a, indicating extraprostatic extension and positive surgical margins. A reassuring finding is that the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The absence of documented nodal sampling means that the pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, which widens the uncertainty regarding regional spread. The biopsy findings documented Acinar adenocarcinoma. Countervailing to the positive margins and extension is the absence of documented lymphovascular invasion. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. Missing nodal sampling limits the staging information available. The fixed estimated horizon is 67.48 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 43.86–91.10 months; its coverage has not been validated.
